The supplier Statement assumes only that a real random variable written X_t-X_s has law N(0,|t-s|); it imposes no Brownian-process hypothesis. It explicitly states E|Z|^(2m)=(2m-1)!! for Z~N(0,1), proved by truncated density integration and integration by parts in steps 1.1-2.1. The already cited normal-law definition represents N(0,v) as the law of sqrt(v) Z, so scaling yields E X_0^4=3v^2. Alternatively take s=0, t=v, Y_0=0, Y_v=X_0 in the supplier. The AR(1) law was established in step 2.1; no construction as a Brownian increment is needed.
